threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, success criteria, and initial backlog for the onboarding rollout.

messages.text: Kickoff for the Hybrid Customer Onboarding Workspace Rollout. Goal: define a standard hybrid onboarding workflow and workspace that sales and project teams can both use without disrupting current deals. For now, let us focus on the onboarding phase from signed contract to handover to steady-state customer success. Anything before contract signature or long-term account growth is not in this first wave. I will use the existing mapping work in T1 and the overview in A1 as our baseline. Can you all react here with any must-have items you think should be in scope, and anything you feel we should explicitly park for later phases?

Thanks for framing this. From my side, I would keep in scope: internal handover from sales to project, initial technical and admin setup, and the first success review after go-live. I would keep renewals, upsell playbooks, and complex custom integrations out of scope for now. For T1, I can help complete interviews with recent project owners so A1 reflects both sales and project views. On success criteria, I suggest we align early with what we will track in T12 and A4 so we do not overcomplicate the sheet.

I want to double-check the boundary. When you say from signed contract to handover, do we include the internal approvals and credit checks that sometimes happen after signature but before kickoff? Also, for the workspace, are we touching CRM configuration at all, or just the shared folders and channels? I am asking so that when we define T2 and T12 we do not promise changes that depend on IT or finance sign-off.

Good questions. Proposal: we include any internal checks that are mandatory before kickoff, but only in terms of tracking them in the workflow, not redesigning finance or risk policies. For the workspace, we stay within existing CRM and office tools, so no new systems or deep CRM reconfiguration in this rollout. That means we can document how to use current CRM fields but not change the schema. If no one objects, I will capture this as our working scope boundary under D1.

From a structure and compliance angle, I would keep in scope the way we store onboarding documents and approvals in the workspace, but not broader document retention policy. We should make sure A1 clearly shows where legal and data protection checks sit in the flow so that later T4 can plug into it. For success metrics, I would like us to track at least one quality indicator, not only speed, otherwise we risk pushing teams to rush through steps.

From the admin side, I suggest we explicitly include in scope: standard email templates, document templates, and internal checklists that office and project teams will use. That maps to T3, T7, and T12, and will feed into A3, A4, and A5. I agree that billing cycles, credit control, and long-term account documentation can be left for a later phase, but we should at least have a placeholder in the workflow so people know where the handover happens.

Let us talk success metrics so we can shape T12 and A4 properly. My proposal: 1) cycle time from contract signature to onboarding completion, 2) number of missing or incorrect documents detected during onboarding, 3) number of rework loops where we have to go back to the customer for corrections, and 4) internal satisfaction from sales and project teams for the new process, maybe via a simple rating per onboarding. Are these realistic to capture in the sheet without adding too much admin overhead?

Those four make sense. For the sheet in A4 under T12, I can set up columns for: customer name, contract date, onboarding start date, onboarding completion date, count of document issues, count of rework loops, and a simple 1 to 5 rating from sales and project. We can add a notes column for any major blockers. This should be manageable if we keep data entry to a few fields per onboarding. I can also add basic data validation so we do not get inconsistent entries.

Agree with the list. To keep it practical, I suggest we start with those four metrics only and avoid adding more until after the pilot. We can always extend A4 once we see how much effort it takes. For internal satisfaction, we can capture one rating from the project lead and one from the sales owner at the end of each onboarding. That should give us enough signal without a full survey.

I like the metrics, but I am a bit worried about how we will measure rework loops consistently. Sometimes we have a long email thread with the customer and it is not obvious what counts as one loop. Maybe we should define in A4 or in the quick-start guide that a rework loop is any time we have to ask the customer to resend or correct information after we thought the step was complete. Otherwise, different project managers might count differently.

Good point on definitions. Let us standardize it as you suggest: a rework loop is when we ask the customer to correct or resend information after we considered that step done. We can document that in A2 and in the notes of A4. Unless there are objections today, I will treat the four metrics we listed as our initial KPI set under D2 so T12 can move forward.

Catching up on the thread. The scope and metrics sound workable from my side. One small suggestion: in A1 and later in T2, can we clearly mark which steps are mandatory for all customers and which are optional depending on deal size or complexity? That will help avoid the workflow becoming too heavy for smaller accounts.

Agreed, we will flag mandatory vs optional steps in A1 and carry that into T2. To wrap this thread up: scope is contract signature to onboarding completion, including internal checks and workspace setup, but excluding CRM redesign, renewals, upsell playbooks, and broader finance policies. Success metrics are cycle time, document issues, rework loops, and internal satisfaction, captured in A4 via T12. I will summarize this in the project brief and move T1 and T12 into active planning.

threads.thread_goal: Design and finalize the target onboarding workflow, RACI, and workspace structure.

messages.text: Sharing the first draft of the target hybrid onboarding workflow and workspace proposal. The flow and RACI are summarized in A1, and the workspace structure and naming rules are in a draft of A6. These are based on the scope and metrics we agreed earlier and will feed into T2, T5, and T6. Please review and comment on any missing steps, unclear responsibilities, or workspace gaps before we lock this for the pilot.

I went through A1 and A6. Overall structure looks coherent, but I see a couple of potential bottlenecks. First, the legal and data protection review step is currently placed after we share some documents with the customer. I would move that earlier in the flow so T4 can happen before any sensitive data is exchanged. Second, in A6, the workspace has separate folders for sales and project, but approvals are scattered. I suggest a single 'Approvals and Sign-offs' area with clear naming, which will also help when we raise A8 tickets for IT access.

On the RACI in A1, I noticed that for the initial kickoff meeting, both sales and project are marked as accountable. To avoid confusion, I would set project as accountable and sales as responsible for the commercial recap. For the workspace in A6, could we add a standard channel for 'Customer Questions and Decisions' so that key decisions are not buried in email? That will also make it easier to reference decisions later when we update A7 after the pilot.

I have a question on the workspace naming rules in A6. For smaller customers, do we still create the full set of folders and channels, or is there a 'light' version? The draft seems to assume the same structure for all deals. I am concerned that for very small accounts, this might feel like overkill and people will revert to ad-hoc tools. Maybe T5 could define a minimal core structure and optional add-ons.

Good call. I propose we define in T5 a core workspace package that is always created, plus optional folders and channels for complex projects. In A6, we can mark these as 'core' and 'optional' and give guidance on when to use each. For the pilot, I suggest we use the full structure so we can test it properly, but we can scale it down later if needed.

From an admin and documentation angle, I like the idea of a single 'Approvals and Sign-offs' area in A6. It will make it easier to file standard templates from A5 and link them to specific onboarding cases. For the workflow in A1, could we add a clear step for creating the KPI entry in A4 at the start of each onboarding? That way, T12 becomes part of the routine rather than an afterthought.

Looking at the RACI in A1, I would also clarify who is responsible for granting workspace access. Right now it is marked as shared between project and IT. To avoid delays, I suggest project is responsible for raising the A8 ticket and IT is accountable for execution. That way, T6 has a clear trigger and we can track delays more easily.

Agree on embedding KPI tracking into the flow. We can add a step in A1 right after workspace creation where the project lead opens a new line in A4. On the workspace structure in A6, I will adjust the hierarchy so that each customer workspace has: 1) General, 2) Customer Questions and Decisions, 3) Approvals and Sign-offs, 4) Internal Planning, and 5) Customer Deliverables, with optional subfolders for complex setups. This should keep navigation simple while covering the main needs.

That structure works for me. For naming conventions in A6, can we standardize on something like 'ONB-CustomerName-YYYY' for the main workspace and then consistent names for channels and folders? It will help reporting later and make it easier for new team members to find things. Also, for the workflow in A1, I am fine with project being accountable for kickoff and workspace setup as long as sales remains clearly responsible for commercial clarifications.

I am ok with using the full structure for the pilot as long as we document in A6 which parts are optional for later. One more question: in A1, the step for internal training on the new process is currently at the very end. Should we move that earlier so that by the time we configure the pilot workspace in T6, the core team has already gone through at least a short briefing?

Yes, training should happen before we start the pilot. I will move that step earlier in A1 and align it with T9. To close on the workflow and RACI: unless there are strong objections by end of day, we will treat the updated A1 as approved for pilot use under D3. That means T2 can be marked as complete once these edits are in.

I will incorporate all the feedback into A6 today: core vs optional structure, standard naming, dedicated approvals area, and the Customer Questions and Decisions channel. Once done, I will confirm with IT that the structure is feasible and that A8 tickets can reference a simple template. After that, we can consider the workspace structure and naming conventions agreed for the pilot under D4.

Great, thanks. To summarize this thread: we have adjusted A1 so legal checks happen earlier, clarified RACI for kickoff and access, embedded KPI tracking, and moved training before the pilot. A6 now defines a simple, consistent workspace structure with core and optional elements and clear naming rules. With D3 and D4 in place, we can proceed to configure the pilot workspace in T6 using the agreed structure.

threads.thread_goal: Create and validate templates, checklists, and compliance aspects.

messages.text: I have posted initial versions of the onboarding templates and checklists. A5 contains the email and document templates drafted under T3, A3 has the internal checklists from T7, and A2 is a first pass at the quick-start guide linked to T8. These are aligned with the workflow in A1 but still need review for clarity and compliance. Please share comments, especially on missing steps, confusing wording, or anything that might conflict with legal or data protection rules.

Thanks for pulling these together. First impressions: the structure of A3 maps well to the workflow steps in A1, and A2 gives a clear overview. One thing I noticed is that some of the customer-facing templates in A5 still use slightly different terminology than the workflow. We should align terms like 'kickoff' vs 'onboarding start' so people do not get confused. Also, we need to make sure T4 sends the right set of templates to legal for review, not just a subset.

From a compliance perspective, I see a couple of items to adjust before we send A5 and A3 to legal under T4. Some templates ask for customer data that might be considered sensitive without clearly stating why it is needed or how it will be used. We should add short explanations and, where relevant, references to our internal policies. Also, in A2, it would help to highlight which steps require legal or data protection checks so users do not skip them under time pressure.

On the checklists in A3, I like that we have separate ones for sales, project, and customer success as per T7. For the project checklist, could we add explicit items for: 1) creating the KPI entry in A4, and 2) confirming that the workspace structure in A6 is set up according to the standard? That will help us keep T12 and T6 consistent without relying on memory.

I have a question on the tone of the customer emails in A5. Some of them sound quite formal, others more casual. Do we have a preferred style? It might be good to define that in A2 so that when people adapt the templates, they stay within a consistent range. Also, for the internal quick-start in A2, could we add a short 'do and do not' section for handling customer data, to reinforce the compliance points?

Good catch on tone. I can standardize the language in A5 to be clear and professional but still friendly, and then add a short style note in A2 so people know how much they can adapt. I will also add a 'do and do not' section on customer data handling, using simple examples. Once I have made these edits and the compliance clarifications suggested earlier, I will bundle A5, A3, and A2 for T4 and send them to legal and data protection for review.

Looking at A3 from a project lead perspective, the sequence is logical. One suggestion: add a final checklist item to confirm that all mandatory documents from A5 are stored in the correct workspace folders as defined in A6. That will help avoid missing files when we later compile A7 for the pilot. Also, maybe we can add a short escalation note in A2 for what to do if legal sign-off is delayed.

Once you have incorporated the feedback, please confirm here so we can trigger T4 formally. For legal review, we should ask them to check: 1) data fields requested in A5, 2) wording around consent and usage, and 3) any references in A2 to internal policies. We will need written confirmation from legal and data protection that the templates are acceptable before we use them in the pilot.

Updates done: terminology aligned with A1, tone standardized, explanations added for sensitive data fields, and 'do and do not' plus escalation paths added to A2. Checklists in A3 now include KPI entry in A4, workspace verification against A6, and confirmation that all mandatory templates from A5 are stored correctly. I have sent A5, A3, and A2 to legal and data protection under T4 with a summary of what we need them to confirm.

I reviewed the updated versions and they look much clearer. From my side, the main remaining risk is making sure legal and data protection explicitly confirm that the data we collect and the way we store it in the workspace comply with our internal rules. Once we have their written sign-off, I would be comfortable saying that our templates and checklists cover the necessary compliance aspects for the pilot.

Legal and data protection have now replied. They requested two minor wording tweaks in A5 around data usage, which I have applied, and confirmed that with those changes, the templates and checklists are acceptable for use in the pilot. I have recorded their confirmation in the version history and noted it in T4 as final sign-off.

Perfect. With legal and data protection confirmation in place, I propose we treat the current versions of A5, A3, and A2 as our standard onboarding templates and guides for the pilot under D5. We will still be able to refine them after we run T10 and T11, but for now they are our baseline.

Given the written confirmation from legal and data protection and the adjustments we made, I am comfortable stating that our onboarding templates, checklists, and quick-start guide now fully reflect the legal and data protection requirements for the pilot. We should still remind teams in A2 to follow the process strictly, but from a design standpoint, I would mark compliance coverage as confirmed under D6.

Thanks all. To wrap this thread: A5, A3, and A2 are now our approved standard templates and guides for the pilot, with legal and data protection sign-off recorded in T4. We will use them as-is during T10 and then revisit them in T11 based on pilot feedback. I will update the change log and make sure links to these artifacts are visible in the workspace structure defined in A6.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and coordinate the pilot onboarding execution and training.

messages.text: Time to plan the pilot. Proposal: we use the next new customer with a signed contract and a hybrid onboarding requirement as our pilot candidate. I have one in mind that is due to sign early next week. For T6, we would configure their workspace using A6 and raise the necessary A8 ticket. In parallel, we need to decide on training format under T9 and align on the pilot start date for T10. Please share any constraints or preferences.

Using the next hybrid customer sounds reasonable. From a scheduling perspective, I would avoid starting the pilot in the last week of the month because of reporting load. If the contract signs early next week, could we target pilot onboarding start for the following Monday? That gives us a few days to complete T6 and run T9. On training format, I lean toward a short live session plus a recording, so people who cannot attend still have access.

I agree with avoiding month-end. For training, I am a bit concerned that a single live session might not be enough for all time zones. Maybe we can do one live session and then rely on A2 as the main reference, with a short Q and A thread in the channel. That way, T9 is covered without needing multiple live slots.

From the admin side, as long as we have at least two working days between contract signature and pilot start, I can prepare the customer-specific folders, checklists from A3, and initial entries in A4 under T6 and T12. For training, I can help by walking through the templates in A5 and the checklists in A3 during the session, so people see how they fit into the workspace defined in A6.

On the workspace side, once we confirm the pilot customer, I will double-check that the structure in A6 is applied correctly and that the A8 ticket includes any special access needs. We should also verify that any legal or data protection conditions specific to this customer are reflected in the templates from A5 before we start T10. If there are unusual requirements, we might need a quick check with legal again.

From a project lead perspective, starting the pilot the Monday after contract signature works for me. I would like the training under T9 to happen at least one day before we start T10, so the team can try out the workspace and ask questions. For the training content, we should walk through A2, show where A3 and A5 live in the workspace, and maybe do a quick demo of filling in A4 for one sample customer.

So far, consensus seems to be: use the next hybrid customer, avoid month-end, and target pilot onboarding start for the Monday after contract signature, with training at least one day before. Unless anyone sees a major issue, I will confirm that customer as our pilot candidate and set that Monday as the planned start date under D7 once the contract is signed.

On training format, I am comfortable with one live session plus a recording, as long as A2 is clearly linked in the invite and in the channel. Maybe we can schedule a 45-minute session: 20 minutes walkthrough, 15 minutes Q and A, 10 minutes for a quick demo in the pilot workspace. That should satisfy T9 without being too heavy.

Agree. One live session plus recording seems like a good balance. We can also add a short FAQ section to A2 after the session based on the questions we get. For scheduling, I suggest mid-week, mid-morning to catch most people. If we record it and share the link in the channel, that should cover those who cannot attend.

Based on the feedback, I propose we decide on the following for training under D8: one 45-minute live session mid-week, mid-morning, recorded and shared, using A2 as the main guide and walking through A3, A5, A4, and the workspace in A6. We will then rely on the recording and A2 for anyone who cannot attend live. If no objections by tomorrow morning, I will lock this in and move T9 into scheduling.

Works for me. Once the pilot customer is confirmed and the date is set, I will prepare the customer-specific workspace content under T6, pre-fill the relevant checklists from A3, and set up the initial KPI line in A4. I will also draft a short invite text for the training that links to A2 and explains what people should expect from the session.

Great. To summarize: we have selected the next hybrid customer as our pilot and will start onboarding on the Monday after contract signature, with training at least one day before. Training will be one live 45-minute session plus recording, using A2, A3, A5, A4, and A6 as the core materials. Workspace configuration under T6 and training under T9 are now our immediate priorities before we execute T10.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot results, adjust process, and agree on rollout plan.

messages.text: We have completed the first pilot onboarding using the new workflow and workspace. A7 contains the pilot onboarding summary report from T10, and A4 has the KPI snapshot. Overall, cycle time was slightly better than our previous average, but we had a few rework loops around missing documents. Let us use this thread to review key findings, propose changes to the workflow and templates, and decide on broader rollout timing.

Looking at A4, the pilot onboarding took 14 days from contract signature to completion, which is about two days faster than our recent average. We had three document-related issues and two rework loops, mostly around proof of address and contact details. Feedback in A7 suggests that the customer found the templates in A5 clear, but some internal users forgot to follow the checklists in A3 consistently, which may explain the rework.

From the project lead side, the workspace structure in A6 worked well. Having a dedicated Approvals and Sign-offs area made it easy to track what was pending. The main friction was that some team members were not sure when to update A4, so KPI entries were done late. Maybe we should emphasize that step more in A2 and in the project checklist in A3.

From a structure and compliance angle, I am pleased that we had no issues raised by legal or data protection during the pilot. A7 notes that all required approvals were stored correctly in the workspace. However, the report also mentions that some optional folders in A6 were created but never used, which added a bit of clutter. For the broader rollout, we might want to simplify the default structure and only add optional elements when clearly needed.

I noticed in A7 that sales feedback on the new process was positive overall, but there were comments about the number of internal steps before the customer kickoff. Do we think we can safely merge or streamline any of those steps in A1 without creating risk? For example, could we combine some of the internal checks into a single pre-kickoff review meeting?

I think we can streamline a bit. Based on A7, the separate internal alignment and risk review meetings often had the same participants and topics. We could merge them into one pre-kickoff session in A1, as long as we keep the checklist items from A3 to ensure nothing is skipped. That should reduce calendar overhead without changing the actual controls.

To address the document issues, I suggest two changes: 1) update A5 to include clearer examples of acceptable proof of address and contact details, and 2) adjust A3 so that the sales checklist explicitly requires verifying these items before handover. We can also add a short reminder in A2 that incomplete documents are a common source of rework, with a tip on how to avoid it.

These sound like sensible adjustments. Let us list the concrete changes we want before broader rollout: 1) merge the two internal pre-kickoff meetings in A1 into one, 2) simplify the default workspace structure in A6 by removing rarely used optional folders, 3) update A5 with clearer examples for key documents, 4) strengthen A3 and A2 around KPI updates and document checks. Once we agree on this set, we can implement them under T11.

I support that list. From the pilot, I do not see any need for major structural changes beyond what you described. The process felt manageable, and the main issues were around habits and clarity, which these tweaks should address. For T11, we should also update A7 with a short section on 'changes decided' so we have a clear record.

I agree with the proposed changes. When simplifying A6, I will keep the core structure intact and move some of the optional folders into a 'create when needed' section in A2 so teams know they exist but do not create them by default. That should reduce clutter while preserving flexibility. I will also double-check that the merged pre-kickoff step in A1 still clearly shows where legal and data protection checks happen.

Sounds good. With this, I suggest we formally agree that these four adjustments are the key changes we will implement before broader rollout under D9. We will capture them in T11, update A1, A6, A5, A3, and A2 accordingly, and log the changes in A7.

Given the pilot results in A4 and the feedback in A7, I would be comfortable moving to a broader rollout once these changes are in place. The process already shows time savings and no major compliance issues. Maybe we can plan a phased rollout over the next month, starting with a few more customers before making it the default for all new onboardings.

I agree with a phased approach. We could, for example, apply the updated process to the next three suitable customers as an extended pilot, monitor A4 for any new issues, and then, if results stay positive, declare it the standard process. That would give teams a bit more time to get used to A2, A3, and A5 before we fully switch over.

Based on the data in A4, the feedback in A7, and your comments, I propose we go ahead with a broader rollout under D10, using a short phased period as you described. Once T11 is complete and the updated artifacts are published, we will apply the process to the next three hybrid onboardings, monitor KPIs, and then make it the default for all new customers unless we see major issues.

I will start implementing the agreed changes under T11: update A5 with clearer examples, adjust A3 and A2 for document checks and KPI updates, and support the updates to A1 and A6. Once done, I will refresh the links in the shared workspace and add a short note in A2 explaining the phased rollout so teams know what to expect.

Thanks everyone. To close this thread: we have reviewed the pilot results in A4 and A7, agreed on a focused set of changes to the workflow, workspace, templates, and checklists under D9, and decided to proceed with a phased broader rollout under D10 once T11 is complete. We will continue to track KPIs in A4 and capture any further learnings in A7 as we onboard the next customers.
